A.description: matcher before D21: one IN-list load of every candidate, validate every patient, one result dict per patient

B.description: D21 step 1: chunked load and match, PreparedQuery, trusted events, integer window checks, SQL comparability; detail='full'

C.description: parallel Python at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 14 workers over chunks (a later change)

D.description: Rust matcher, single-threaded and batched, including FFI (a later change, built only if B+C misses the target)

D'.description: Rust matcher, parallel (a later change, same condition)

limitations: One machine (see environment); no other hardware, operating system or storage was measured.
The data are synthetic and replicated beyond 10,000 distinct patients (see the scaling report): candidate sets and outcomes scale as exact multiples, which a real population would not.

Queries are the scaling benchmark's seeded random queries (10 at 100,000 patients and above), not a clinical mix; percentiles over 10 queries rest on few samples, and the maximum is the slowest single query.

Arm A is the code of the stated git ref extracted and imported from a scratch directory; both arms read the same snapshot files. The snapshots were built by the builder at the ref the report states, not by the final tree.

Peak memory is the query process's maximum resident set size. It includes the interpreter, DuckDB buffers, the caller's windows dictionary (one entry per patient, rebuilt for each query) and the full result, which for detail='full' is one dict per patient and is part of what the caller asked for.

"Engine-only" time is the seconds inside `trajectory_graph` match calls as measured by a wrapper (about 0.1 microsecond of overhead per call); "end-to-end" is the whole `match` call including candidates(), loading, comparability, exclusions and the context digests.
Latencies are wall-clock times of one Python thread and one DuckDB thread; no tuning was attempted.

Byte identity is checked by a digest of canonical JSON of the plan, candidate count, counts and every patient result (not the context block, whose snapshot and code digests change with the code); no exhaustive reference ran at scale.
Arms C, D and D' have not been run.
